items.project_definition: The structured set of endpoints operating under the v1 namespace to facilitate communication between clients and the server.
A validation rule that prohibits the removal of an educational offering if it currently contains registered participants.
The security process of verifying identity via bearer tokens passed in the request header.
An asynchronous operation executed independently of the main request-response cycle, such as triggering transactional emails.
A formal constraint governing the allowable state transitions or operations within the system logic.
The protocol governing cross-origin resource sharing to allow secure access from diverse browser domains.
The application of bcrypt to transform plaintext passwords into irreversible fixed-length strings for secure storage.
A standardized payload containing an array of failure details, codes, and messages when an operation cannot be completed.
A relational pointer that enforces referential integrity between two data entities.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for all request and response bodies.
A compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties as a bearer token.
A logical negation operator indicating that a specific side effect must not impede the delivery of the primary response.
The technical documentation mapping defining the structural properties and types of the system entities.
The incoming data payload and headers sent by a client to initiate a specific server-side operation.
The outgoing payload sent from the server, wrapped in a consistent envelope containing data and metadata.
A classification assigned to a user, such as student or instructor, which determines access permissions and available actions.
The 128-bit universally unique identifier used as the primary key for all system entities.
